17	/-- An exact rational `num / den` with `den > 0`, kept in lowest terms by `mk'`; `Q.eq` is
18	    equality by value for the rare unreduced literal. -/
19	structure Q where
20	  num : Int
21	  den : Nat
22	  den_pos : den > 0 := by decide
23	  deriving Repr
24	
25	namespace Q
26	
27	/-- Structural equality (same numerator and denominator); `Q.eq` is equality by value. -/
28	instance : DecidableEq Q := fun a b =>
29	  if h : a.num = b.num ∧ a.den = b.den then
30	    isTrue (by
31	      obtain ⟨n₁, d₁, p₁⟩ := a
32	      obtain ⟨n₂, d₂, p₂⟩ := b
33	      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
34	      simp only at h1 h2
35	      subst h1; subst h2; rfl)
36	  else isFalse (by intro e; subst e; exact h ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)
37	
38	def ofInt (n : Int) : Q := ⟨n, 1, by decide⟩
39	def zero : Q := ofInt 0
40	instance : Inhabited Q := ⟨zero⟩
41	
42	/-- `a / b` in lowest terms for a positive natural `b`; a zero `b` is treated as one so the value
43	    stays total. Reducing here keeps chained products and sums from growing without bound. -/
44	def mk' (a : Int) (b : Nat) : Q :=
45	  if h : b > 0 then
46	    let g := Nat.gcd a.natAbs b
47	    have hg : 0 < g := Nat.gcd_pos_of_pos_right _ h
48	    ⟨a / (g : Int), b / g, Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd h (Nat.gcd_dvd_right _ _)) hg⟩
49	  else ⟨a, 1, by decide⟩
50	
51	def le (a b : Q) : Bool := a.num * (b.den : Int) ≤ b.num * (a.den : Int)
52	def lt (a b : Q) : Bool := a.num * (b.den : Int) < b.num * (a.den : Int)
53	def eq (a b : Q) : Bool := a.num * (b.den : Int) = b.num * (a.den : Int)
54	def ge (a b : Q) : Bool := le b a
55	def gt (a b : Q) : Bool := lt b a
56	
57	def add (a b : Q) : Q := mk' (a.num * b.den + b.num * a.den) (a.den * b.den)
58	def sub (a b : Q) : Q := mk' (a.num * b.den - b.num * a.den) (a.den * b.den)
59	def mul (a b : Q) : Q := mk' (a.num * b.num) (a.den * b.den)
60	def neg (a : Q) : Q := ⟨-a.num, a.den, a.den_pos⟩
61	def abs (a : Q) : Q := ⟨if a.num < 0 then -a.num else a.num, a.den, a.den_pos⟩
62	/-- `a / b`; division by zero yields zero (the callers guard it and report `unknown`). -/
63	def div (a b : Q) : Q :=
64	  if b.num = 0 then zero
65	  else if b.num > 0 then mk' (a.num * b.den) (a.den * b.num.toNat)
66	  else mk' (-(a.num * b.den)) (a.den * (-b.num).toNat)
67	def half (a : Q) : Q := mk' a.num (a.den * 2)
68	def min (a b : Q) : Q := if le a b then a else b

70	def isZero (a : Q) : Bool := a.num = 0

78	end Q

82	  | 0, _, x => x
83	  | fuel + 1, n, x =>
84	    if x = 0 then 0
85	    else
86	      let y := (x + n / x) / 2
87	      if y ≥ x then x else isqrtAux fuel n y
88

92	theorem isqrt_one : isqrt 1 = 1 := rfl

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Units
  Exact quantities.

  A statute states feet, inches, miles and miles per hour; another states metres and
  kilometres per hour; a scene states metres and metres per second. None of these convert
  to a common INTEGER unit exactly (a kilometre per hour is 5/18 of a metre per second), so
  quantities are exact rationals over SI base units: metre, second, metre per second,
  metre per second squared, degree. No `Float` anywhere; comparison is by cross-multiplication.

  This is the only file where a unit of law meets a unit of measurement. A rule may write a
  number only as the argument of one of the constructors below (the gate enforces this), so a
  threshold in a rule and the same threshold in a label cannot round differently.
-/
namespace TrafficSpec

/-- An exact rational `num / den` with `den > 0`, kept in lowest terms by `mk'`; `Q.eq` is
    equality by value for the rare unreduced literal. -/
structure Q where
  num : Int
  den : Nat
  den_pos : den > 0 := by decide
  deriving Repr

namespace Q

/-- Structural equality (same numerator and denominator); `Q.eq` is equality by value. -/
instance : DecidableEq Q := fun a b =>
  if h : a.num = b.num ∧ a.den = b.den then
    isTrue (by
      obtain ⟨n₁, d₁, p₁⟩ := a
      obtain ⟨n₂, d₂, p₂⟩ := b
      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
      simp only at h1 h2
      subst h1; subst h2; rfl)
  else isFalse (by intro e; subst e; exact h ⟨rfl, rfl⟩)

def ofInt (n : Int) : Q := ⟨n, 1, by decide⟩
def zero : Q := ofInt 0
instance : Inhabited Q := ⟨zero⟩

/-- `a / b` in lowest terms for a positive natural `b`; a zero `b` is treated as one so the value
    stays total. Reducing here keeps chained products and sums from growing without bound. -/
def mk' (a : Int) (b : Nat) : Q :=
  if h : b > 0 then
    let g := Nat.gcd a.natAbs b
    have hg : 0 < g := Nat.gcd_pos_of_pos_right _ h
    ⟨a / (g : Int), b / g, Nat.div_pos (Nat.le_of_dvd h (Nat.gcd_dvd_right _ _)) hg⟩
  else ⟨a, 1, by decide⟩

def le (a b : Q) : Bool := a.num * (b.den : Int) ≤ b.num * (a.den : Int)
def lt (a b : Q) : Bool := a.num * (b.den : Int) < b.num * (a.den : Int)
def eq (a b : Q) : Bool := a.num * (b.den : Int) = b.num * (a.den : Int)
def ge (a b : Q) : Bool := le b a
def gt (a b : Q) : Bool := lt b a

def add (a b : Q) : Q := mk' (a.num * b.den + b.num * a.den) (a.den * b.den)
def sub (a b : Q) : Q := mk' (a.num * b.den - b.num * a.den) (a.den * b.den)
def mul (a b : Q) : Q := mk' (a.num * b.num) (a.den * b.den)
def neg (a : Q) : Q := ⟨-a.num, a.den, a.den_pos⟩
def abs (a : Q) : Q := ⟨if a.num < 0 then -a.num else a.num, a.den, a.den_pos⟩
/-- `a / b`; division by zero yields zero (the callers guard it and report `unknown`). -/
def div (a b : Q) : Q :=
  if b.num = 0 then zero
  else if b.num > 0 then mk' (a.num * b.den) (a.den * b.num.toNat)
  else mk' (-(a.num * b.den)) (a.den * (-b.num).toNat)
def half (a : Q) : Q := mk' a.num (a.den * 2)
def min (a b : Q) : Q := if le a b then a else b
def max (a b : Q) : Q := if le a b then b else a
def isZero (a : Q) : Bool := a.num = 0
def isNonneg (a : Q) : Bool := a.num ≥ 0

instance : Add Q := ⟨add⟩
instance : Sub Q := ⟨sub⟩
instance : Mul Q := ⟨mul⟩
instance : Neg Q := ⟨neg⟩

end Q

/-- Integer square root (floor), by Newton's iteration from `n` with fuel; exact for all `n`. -/
def isqrtAux : Nat → Nat → Nat → Nat
  | 0, _, x => x
  | fuel + 1, n, x =>
    if x = 0 then 0
    else
      let y := (x + n / x) / 2
      if y ≥ x then x else isqrtAux fuel n y

def isqrt (n : Nat) : Nat := if n < 2 then n else isqrtAux 256 n n

theorem isqrt_zero : isqrt 0 = 0 := rfl
theorem isqrt_one : isqrt 1 = 1 := rfl

namespace Units

-- Lengths (metres).
def metres (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt n
def centimetres (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' n 100
def millimetres (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' n 1000
/-- Micrometres: the integer unit adapters use for measured lengths. -/
def micrometres (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' n 1000000
def kilometres (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt (n * 1000)
def inches (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' (n * 254) 10000          -- 25.4 mm exactly
def feet (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' (n * 3048) 10000           -- 304.8 mm exactly
def yards (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' (n * 9144) 10000
def miles (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' (n * 1609344) 1000        -- 1609.344 m exactly

-- Durations (seconds).
def seconds (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt n
def milliseconds (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' n 1000
def minutes (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt (n * 60)
def hours (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt (n * 3600)

-- Speeds (metres per second).
def metresPerSecond (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt n
/-- Micrometres per second: the integer unit adapters use for measured speeds. -/
def micrometresPerSecond (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' n 1000000
def kmh (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' (n * 1000) 3600              -- exactly 5/18 m/s per km/h
def mph (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' (n * 44704) 100000           -- 0.44704 m/s exactly

-- Curvatures (per metre).
def perMetre (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt n

-- Accelerations (metres per second squared).
def metresPerSecondSq (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt n
def micrometresPerSecondSq (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' n 1000000

-- Angles (degrees) and rates (degrees per second).
def degrees (n : Int) : Q := Q.ofInt n
def millidegrees (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' n 1000

-- Dimensionless.
def ratio (a : Int) (b : Nat) : Q := Q.mk' a b
def percent (n : Int) : Q := Q.mk' n 100

end Units
end TrafficSpec

inductive PUnit'
  | metre | second | metrePerSecond | metrePerSecondSq | degree | degreePerSecond | perMetre | ratio | count
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

structure ParamValue where
  name : ParamName
  value : Q
  unit : PUnit'
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

structure Operationalization where
  standard : String            -- the clause's words for the standard
  concepts : List String       -- the `drv.*` and atom ids that bound it (one standard may pair several)

    for a law-local definition): the road-user classes (`ru.*` ids) its definition includes, and those
    it leaves unresolved. Every other class is excluded. An aggregate never lists another aggregate. -/

  id : String

  deriving Repr, Inhabited

  params : List ParamValue := []
  aggregates : List LegalAggregate := []
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Rule
  What a specification is: binders with class formulas, an applicability and an obligation, and
  the declarations a reviewer needs (parameters, assumptions, declared intentions,
  operationalizations, residues, narrowings, the rules it composes, the surrogate flag).

  A residue is a span of the text the rule does not capture at all; the plan declares it and the
  rule repeats it verbatim. A narrowing is a reading the coder chose on a span the plan does
  carry, stated here so the review judges the rule as it is: the span it names and why. The
  coder may add narrowings and never residues.

  Applicability and obligation are two formulas because a rule whose situation never arises is
  not compliant, it is not engaged: `notApplicable` is a verdict of its own, the witness check can
  demand a scenario for it, and a monitor reads the applicability as the trigger and the
  obligation as what to verify once triggered.

  A surrogate rule (the whole duty is an operationalized standard) is monitored like any other,
  but its verdicts are evidence about the standard, never the law's own verdict; the flag is what
  the monitor and the export propagate so the two are never summed.

  This file holds the declarations only and imports no evaluator: a rule file that imports it
  can state a rule but cannot read a scene, evaluate a formula or build evidence. Evaluation and
  the static check are in RuleEval.lean, which nothing under Rules/ may import.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.Formula
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Unknown

namespace TrafficSpec

/-- A binder: a variable and the class formula (over `ru_*` atoms and class-level derived
    concepts) a track must satisfy to be bound to it. The subject comes first. -/
structure Binder where
  name : String
  cls : Formula
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

/-- A reading chosen on a span the record carries, declared where it is made: the span (a
    segmentation id for a rule, a run of the contract's words for a concept) and what the formulas
    state more narrowly than the words. `kind` is `reading` where the words leave the choice open,
    `observable_reading` where a word with no observable counterpart is read through the conduct
    or the feature it refers to, `no_atom` or `no_operator` where the vocabulary or the language
    cannot state the words — a declaration the gate returns for a gap, never a reading the rule
    stands on. -/
structure Narrowing where
  span : String
  why : String
  kind : String := "reading"
  deriving Repr, Inhabited, DecidableEq

structure Rule where
  id : String                                   -- the node id, derived from the law id
  laws : List String                            -- the corpus ids this rule formalizes
  binders : List Binder
  applicability : Formula
  obligation : Formula
  assumptions : List AsmId := []
  intentions : List IntId := []                 -- the declared intentions its formulas read
  operationalizations : List Operationalization := []
  residues : List String := []                  -- what the text says and the rule does not capture
  narrowings : List Narrowing := []             -- readings the coder chose on carried spans
  surrogate : Bool := false
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

inductive Verdict
  | violated
  | compliant
  | notApplicable
  | unknown (why : List UnknownReason)
  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited

namespace Verdict
def tag : Verdict → String
  | .violated => "violated"
  | .compliant => "compliant"
  | .notApplicable => "not_applicable"
  | .unknown _ => "unknown"
def reasons : Verdict → List UnknownReason
  | .unknown w => w
  | _ => []
instance : ToString Verdict := ⟨tag⟩
end Verdict

/-- Kleene combination of the two formulas: not engaged ↦ notApplicable, engaged and the
    obligation decided ↦ compliant/violated, anything undecided ↦ unknown with its reasons. -/
def verdictAt (app obl : R) : Verdict :=
  match app.v with
  | .f => .notApplicable
  | .u => .unknown app.why
  | .t =>
    match obl.v with
    | .t => .compliant
    | .f => .violated
    | .u => .unknown obl.why

theorem verdictAt_notApplicable (app obl : R) (h : app.v = .f) : verdictAt app obl = .notApplicable := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [h]
theorem verdictAt_violated (app obl : R) (ha : app.v = .t) (ho : obl.v = .f) : verdictAt app obl = .violated := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [ha, ho]
theorem verdictAt_compliant (app obl : R) (ha : app.v = .t) (ho : obl.v = .t) : verdictAt app obl = .compliant := by
  unfold verdictAt; rw [ha, ho]

namespace Rule
/-- The formulas a rule consists of, class formulas first. -/
def formulas (r : Rule) : List Formula := r.binders.map (·.cls) ++ [r.applicability, r.obligation]
/-- Atom, primitive and concept names the rule reads. -/
def atoms (r : Rule) : List String := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.atoms).eraseDups
/-- Reading parameters the rule names. -/
def params (r : Rule) : List ParamName := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.params).eraseDups
/-- Rules the rule composes. -/
def composes (r : Rule) : List String := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.composed).eraseDups
/-- Assumptions the formulas read. -/
def usedAssumptions (r : Rule) : List AsmId := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.assumptions).eraseDups
/-- Declared intentions the formulas read. -/
def usedIntentions (r : Rule) : List IntId := (r.formulas.flatMap Formula.intentions).eraseDups
def binderNames (r : Rule) : List String := r.binders.map (·.name)
def subject (r : Rule) : Option String := r.binders.head?.map (·.name)

/-- The rule and, transitively, the rules it composes (each once). -/
def closure (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : List Rule :=
  let rec go (fuel : Nat) (seen : List String) (todo : List Rule) : List Rule :=
    match fuel, todo with
    | 0, _ | _, [] => []
    | fuel + 1, x :: rest =>
      let next := x.composes.filterMap fun id =>
        if seen.contains id then none else rules.find? (·.id == id)
      x :: go fuel (seen ++ next.map (·.id)) (rest ++ next)
  go (rules.length + 1) [r.id] [r]

/-- Whether the rule reads a declared intention, in its own formulas or through a rule it
    composes at any depth. -/
def readsIntention (rules : List Rule) (r : Rule) : Bool :=
  (closure rules r).any fun x => !x.usedIntentions.isEmpty
end Rule

end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders
3	  Scenarios for witnesses and tests: a scene and a trace from a few named quantities, padding by
4	  timestamp, masking under a manifest, and the `Scenario` a witness file declares.
5	
6	  A witness must be indistinguishable from adapter output to an atom, so everything here goes
7	  through the `World` constructors and nothing else. Reachable from `Witness/**` and `Tests/**`
8	  only: a rule that could build its own evidence proves nothing.
9	
10	  No default magnitude lives here — every extent, speed and distance is an argument the witness
11	  writes through a `Units` constructor.
12	-/
13	import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor
14	
15	namespace TrafficSpec
16	namespace Build
17	
18	/-- Cardinal unit headings in the world frame (+x east, +y north). -/
19	def east : Vec := (Q.ofInt 1, Q.zero)
20	def west : Vec := (Q.ofInt (-1), Q.zero)
21	def north : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt 1)
22	def south : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt (-1))
23	
24	def scale (h : Vec) (k : Q) : Vec := (Q.mul h.1 k, Q.mul h.2 k)
25	
26	/-- A road user with position, heading and speed; velocity follows the heading, path length
27	    is the caller's (cumulative) figure, extents are half-length/half-width/half-height. -/
28	def user (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) (heading : Vec) (speed : Q)
29	    (halfExtent : Q × Q × Q) (pathLength : Option Q := none) : RoadUser :=
30	  { track := track
31	    classes := some classes
32	    kin := { position := some pos
33	             heading := some heading
34	             velocity := some (scale heading speed)
35	             speed := some speed
36	             extent := some halfExtent
37	             pathLength := pathLength } }
38	
39	/-- A road user of which only the position (and classes) was observed. -/
40	def sparseUser (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) : RoadUser :=
41	  { track := track, classes := some classes, kin := { position := some pos } }
42

105	def trace (n : Nat) (t0 : Timestamp) (dt : Q) (f : Nat → Timestamp → Scene) : Trace :=

117	    let nb := ((Q.div before dt).num / (Q.div before dt).den).toNat
118	    let na := ((Q.div after dt).num / (Q.div after dt).den).toNat
119	    let pre := (List.range nb).reverse.map fun k => { first with t := first.t - step * (k + 1) }
120	    let post := (List.range na).map fun k => { last with t := last.t + step * (k + 1) }
121	    pre ++ τ ++ post
122	  | _, _ => τ

127	def manifest (absent : List String := []) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=

129	  { full with entries := full.entries.map fun (id, c) => if absent.contains id then (id, .absent) else (id, c) }

134	    about (binder ↦ track) and the episode verdict the plan declared over `window` (a closed range
135	    of timestamps; the whole trace when absent). A lookback window is truncated at the start of
136	    every finite trace, so a witness about a rule with one names the instants it speaks about.
137	    A witness is a test of the rule, not evidence about the law: it shows the formulas reach the
138	    verdict it names, on a scene its author built. A history-boundary witness (`boundary` names the
139	    history its trace lacks) shows that the rule stays unknown where the trace does not reach back

141	structure Scenario where

143	  rule : String

146	  manifest : Manifest

157	def pastOps : List String :=
158	  ["since", "since_rise", "rises", "once", "holdsFor", "atLast", "count", "distance_while", "prim_heading_change",

162	    the verdict is reached for the reason the witness is about: a `notApplicable` witness needs an
163	    instant at which every bound track is present (a track that never appears leaves any rule not
164	    engaged); an `unknown` witness must be unknown only for atoms its manifest masks (an unbound
165	    variable, a truncated window or a missing parameter is a defect, not a masked observation),
166	    except that a history-boundary witness is unknown for a window truncated at the start of its
167	    trace, at least once, and otherwise only for masked atoms; a boundary is declared on an
168	    `unknown` witness only.
169	    The rules are evaluated with their concept calls expanded over `concepts`. A trace the
170	    admission rejects, or a region formal given a region no scene of the trace holds, fails. -/
171	def run (rules : List Rule) (sc : Scenario) (concepts : List Concept := []) : Except String Verdict := do
172	  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule concepts)
173	  let r ← match rules.find? (·.id == sc.rule) with

175	    | none => throw s!"{sc.name}: rule {sc.rule} is not registered"
176	  let S ← match Grounding.Setup.admit rules (maskTrace sc.manifest sc.trace) sc.reading sc.manifest.reidGap with

180	    if !(sc.trace.any fun s => (s.structure? reg).isSome) then
181	      throw s!"{sc.name}: region formal `{n}` is region {reg}, which is no structure of the trace"
182	  let g : Grounding.Grounding := ⟨sc.grounding.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Grounding.canon S.cm t)), sc.regions⟩

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Evidence.Builders
  Scenarios for witnesses and tests: a scene and a trace from a few named quantities, padding by
  timestamp, masking under a manifest, and the `Scenario` a witness file declares.

  A witness must be indistinguishable from adapter output to an atom, so everything here goes
  through the `World` constructors and nothing else. Reachable from `Witness/**` and `Tests/**`
  only: a rule that could build its own evidence proves nothing.

  No default magnitude lives here — every extent, speed and distance is an argument the witness
  writes through a `Units` constructor.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Monitor

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Build

/-- Cardinal unit headings in the world frame (+x east, +y north). -/
def east : Vec := (Q.ofInt 1, Q.zero)
def west : Vec := (Q.ofInt (-1), Q.zero)
def north : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt 1)
def south : Vec := (Q.zero, Q.ofInt (-1))

def scale (h : Vec) (k : Q) : Vec := (Q.mul h.1 k, Q.mul h.2 k)

/-- A road user with position, heading and speed; velocity follows the heading, path length
    is the caller's (cumulative) figure, extents are half-length/half-width/half-height. -/
def user (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) (heading : Vec) (speed : Q)
    (halfExtent : Q × Q × Q) (pathLength : Option Q := none) : RoadUser :=
  { track := track
    classes := some classes
    kin := { position := some pos
             heading := some heading
             velocity := some (scale heading speed)
             speed := some speed
             extent := some halfExtent
             pathLength := pathLength } }

/-- A road user of which only the position (and classes) was observed. -/
def sparseUser (track : TrackId) (classes : List RoadUserClass) (pos : Vec) : RoadUser :=
  { track := track, classes := some classes, kin := { position := some pos } }

def withSignals (u : RoadUser) (f : Signals → Signals) : RoadUser := { u with sig := f u.sig }
def withKin (u : RoadUser) (f : Kin → Kin) : RoadUser := { u with kin := f u.kin }
/-- A measured relation from `a` to `b`, with the measured fields the source supplies. -/
def relation (a b : TrackId) (f : MeasuredRelation → MeasuredRelation := id) : MeasuredRelation := f { a := a, b := b }
def withRelations (s : Scene) (rs : List MeasuredRelation) : Scene := { s with relations := rs }

/-- A region of a kind with a polygon boundary. -/
def region (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (boundary : List Vec) : Structure :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, boundary := some boundary }
/-- An axis-aligned rectangular region from two corners. -/
def rect (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (x0 y0 x1 y1 : Q) : Structure :=
  region id kind [(x0, y0), (x1, y0), (x1, y1), (x0, y1)]
/-- A lane with its direction and neighbours. -/
def lane (id : RegionId) (boundary : List Vec) (direction : Vec)
    (left right : Option RegionId := none) (ordinal count : Option Nat := none)
    (leadsTo : Option (List RegionId) := none) (enters : Option RegionId := none) : Structure :=
  { id := id
    kind := .lane
    boundary := some boundary
    lane := some { direction := some direction, leftNeighbour := left, rightNeighbour := right,
                   ordinalFromLeft := ordinal, countInDirection := count, leadsTo := leadsTo,
                   entersIntersection := enters } }
def point (id : RegionId) (kind : StructureKind) (pos : Vec) : Structure :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, position := some pos }

def device (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) (pos : Option Vec := none) : Device :=
  { id := id, kind := kind, governs := governs, position := pos }
def signal (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (shows : List SignalIndication) : Device :=
  { device id .trafficSignal governs with indications := some shows }
def sign (id : DeviceId) (kind : DeviceKind) (governs : List RegionId) : Device := device id kind governs
def speedLimit (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (value : Q) (kind : SpeedSignKind) : Device :=
  { device id .speedLimitSign governs with speedValue := some value, speedKind := some kind }
def zoneSign (id : DeviceId) (governs : List RegionId) (kind : ZoneKind) (isEnd : Bool)
    (conditions : Option Conditions := none) : Device :=
  { device id .zoneSign governs with zoneKind := some kind, isEnd := some isEnd, conditions := conditions }

/-- Occupancy from the geometry: every user inside every region whose boundary contains its position. -/
def occupancyFromGeometry (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure) : List (TrackId × RegionId) :=
  users.flatMap fun u =>
    match u.kin.position with
    | none => []
    | some p => structures.filterMap fun st =>
      match st.boundary with
      | some poly => if Geom.inPolygon p poly then some (u.track, st.id) else none
      | none => none

/-- A scene; occupancy is derived from geometry unless given. -/
def scene (t : Timestamp) (subject : Option TrackId) (users : List RoadUser) (structures : List Structure)
    (devices : List Device) (occupies : Option (List (TrackId × RegionId)) := none)
    (env : Env := {}) (assumptions : List (AsmId × Bool) := []) (intents : List DeclaredIntent := []) : Scene :=
  { t := t
    subject := subject
    users := users
    structures := structures
    devices := devices
    occupancyObserved := users.map (·.track)
    occupies := occupies.getD (occupancyFromGeometry users structures)
    env := env
    assumptions := assumptions
    intents := intents }

/-- A trace from a scene generator over instants `t0, t0 + dt, …` (`dt` in seconds). -/
def trace (n : Nat) (t0 : Timestamp) (dt : Q) (f : Nat → Timestamp → Scene) : Trace :=
  (List.range n).map fun k =>
    let t : Timestamp := t0 + (Q.mul (Q.ofInt (Int.ofNat k)) (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000))).num /
      (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
    f k t

/-- Repeat the first and last scenes for `before`/`after` seconds at spacing `dt`, so that windows
    at the ends of the interesting part are covered rather than truncated. -/
def pad (τ : Trace) (before after dt : Q) : Trace :=
  match τ.head?, τ.getLast? with
  | some first, some last =>
    let step : Timestamp := (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).num / (Q.mul dt (Q.ofInt 1000)).den
    let nb := ((Q.div before dt).num / (Q.div before dt).den).toNat
    let na := ((Q.div after dt).num / (Q.div after dt).den).toNat
    let pre := (List.range nb).reverse.map fun k => { first with t := first.t - step * (k + 1) }
    let post := (List.range na).map fun k => { last with t := last.t + step * (k + 1) }
    pre ++ τ ++ post
  | _, _ => τ

def masked (m : Manifest) (τ : Trace) : Trace := maskTrace m τ

/-- A manifest that observes every atom except the listed ids (for a `blind` witness). -/
def manifest (absent : List String := []) (gap : Q := Q.zero) : Manifest :=
  let full := Manifest.full "witness" gap
  { full with entries := full.entries.map fun (id, c) => if absent.contains id then (id, .absent) else (id, c) }

end Build

/-- A witness: a rule, a trace, the reading and manifest it assumes, the grounding it speaks
    about (binder ↦ track) and the episode verdict the plan declared over `window` (a closed range
    of timestamps; the whole trace when absent). A lookback window is truncated at the start of
    every finite trace, so a witness about a rule with one names the instants it speaks about.
    A witness is a test of the rule, not evidence about the law: it shows the formulas reach the
    verdict it names, on a scene its author built. A history-boundary witness (`boundary` names the
    history its trace lacks) shows that the rule stays unknown where the trace does not reach back
    far enough to decide it. -/
structure Scenario where
  name : String
  rule : String
  trace : Trace
  reading : Reading
  manifest : Manifest
  grounding : List (String × TrackId)
  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []   -- an instance's region formals, each a region of the trace
  expected : Verdict
  window : Option (Timestamp × Timestamp) := none
  boundary : String := ""
  deriving Repr, Inhabited

namespace Scenario
/-- The operators that look back from the observation they judge, by the tag their truncation at the
    start of a trace carries: only these leave a history-boundary witness unknown. -/
def pastOps : List String :=
  ["since", "since_rise", "rises", "once", "holdsFor", "atLast", "count", "distance_while", "prim_heading_change",
   "heading_since"]

/-- The witness holds when the rule's episode verdict on its grounding has the expected tag, and
    the verdict is reached for the reason the witness is about: a `notApplicable` witness needs an
    instant at which every bound track is present (a track that never appears leaves any rule not
    engaged); an `unknown` witness must be unknown only for atoms its manifest masks (an unbound
    variable, a truncated window or a missing parameter is a defect, not a masked observation),
    except that a history-boundary witness is unknown for a window truncated at the start of its
    trace, at least once, and otherwise only for masked atoms; a boundary is declared on an
    `unknown` witness only.
    The rules are evaluated with their concept calls expanded over `concepts`. A trace the
    admission rejects, or a region formal given a region no scene of the trace holds, fails. -/
def run (rules : List Rule) (sc : Scenario) (concepts : List Concept := []) : Except String Verdict := do
  let rules := rules.map (Concept.expandRule concepts)
  let r ← match rules.find? (·.id == sc.rule) with
    | some r => pure r
    | none => throw s!"{sc.name}: rule {sc.rule} is not registered"
  let S ← match Grounding.Setup.admit rules (maskTrace sc.manifest sc.trace) sc.reading sc.manifest.reidGap with
    | .ok S => pure S
    | .error ds => throw s!"{sc.name}: the trace is not admitted: {"; ".intercalate ds}"
  for (n, reg) in sc.regions do
    if !(sc.trace.any fun s => (s.structure? reg).isSome) then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: region formal `{n}` is region {reg}, which is no structure of the trace"
  let g : Grounding.Grounding := ⟨sc.grounding.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Grounding.canon S.cm t)), sc.regions⟩
  let tl := Grounding.evaluate S r g
  let rows := tl.verdicts.toList.filter fun (t, _) =>
    match sc.window with
    | some (a, b) => a ≤ t && t ≤ b
    | none => true
  let got := Grounding.episode (rows.map (·.2))
  if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && sc.expected.tag != "unknown" then
    throw s!"{sc.name}: a history boundary is declared on a witness that expects {sc.expected.tag}, not unknown"
  if got.tag != sc.expected.tag then
    throw s!"{sc.name}: expected {sc.expected.tag}, got {got.tag} {(got.reasons.map UnknownReason.tag)}"
  match sc.expected with
  | .notApplicable =>
    if tl.present then pure got
    else throw s!"{sc.name}: not applicable, but no instant has every bound track present"
  | .unknown _ =>
    let absent := sc.manifest.absentIds
    let truncated := fun (w : UnknownReason) => match w with | .windowTruncated op => pastOps.contains op | _ => false
    let stray := got.reasons.filter fun w => match w with
      | .absentAtom n => !(atomIdOf n).any absent.contains
      | w => sc.boundary.isEmpty || !truncated w
    if !stray.isEmpty then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: unknown for {(stray.map UnknownReason.tag)}, not for an atom the manifest masks{if sc.boundary.isEmpty then "" else " or a window truncated at the trace start"}"
    else if !sc.boundary.isEmpty && !got.reasons.any truncated then
      throw s!"{sc.name}: a history-boundary witness, but no window is truncated at the trace start"
    else pure got
  | _ => pure got
end Scenario

end TrafficSpec

1	/-
2	  TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Time
3	  Metric windows without a frame rate.
4	
5	  Every observation carries a timestamp; a body also carries the path length it has travelled.
6	  A window is measured in one of the two: a duration of time, or a length of path travelled.
7	  Semantics are defined on the OBSERVED instants only; the one interpolation-free precondition is
8	  adequacy: a window of length d over a span is adequate when consecutive observations in the
9	  span are at most d/2 apart. An inadequate span yields `unknown`
10	  with the reason `samplingGap`, never a verdict invented between frames.
11	
12	  Windows are computed for every instant of a trace at once: positions are monotone, so the
13	  window boundary moves one way and a two-pointer sweep with a range-maximum table over the gaps
14	  gives every window in O(n log n).
15	
16	  There is no `next`, no rate and no frame count anywhere in the library.
17	-/
18	import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Units
19	
20	namespace TrafficSpec
21	
22	/-- Milliseconds, monotone within a trace. -/
23	abbrev Timestamp := Int
24	
25	/-- Which quantity a window is measured in. -/
26	inductive Measure
27	  | time | path
28	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited
29	
30	/-- A window: a non-negative length in seconds (time) or metres (path). -/
31	structure Duration where
32	  measure : Measure
33	  length : Q
34	  deriving Repr
35	
36	namespace Duration
37	def time (q : Q) : Duration := ⟨.time, q⟩
38	def path (q : Q) : Duration := ⟨.path, q⟩
39	end Duration
40	
41	namespace Time
42	
43	def ofTimestamp (t : Timestamp) : Q := Units.milliseconds t
44	
45	/-- Consecutive gaps of a sorted list of positions (time or path). -/
46	def gaps : List Q → List Q
47	  | a :: b :: rest => Q.sub b a :: gaps (b :: rest)
48	  | _ => []
49	
50	/-- Every consecutive gap in the span is at most `d / 2`. Vacuously true on one observation. -/
51	def adequate (d : Q) (span : List Q) : Bool :=
52	  (gaps span).all (fun g => Q.le g (Q.half d))
53	
54	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
55	-- Range maximum over the gaps between consecutive observed positions (sparse table).
56	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	/-- `gapMax.query lo hi` is the largest gap `pos[k] - pos[k-1]` for `lo < k ≤ hi`, given that
58	    every position in `[lo, hi]` is observed. -/
59	structure GapMax where
60	  table : Array (Array Q)      -- table[k][j] = max of gaps[j .. j + 2^k)
61	  gapsArr : Array Q            -- gapsArr[k] = pos[k+1] - pos[k], or zero where a side is missing
62	
63	namespace GapMax
64	def log2 (n : Nat) : Nat := if n ≤ 1 then 0 else 1 + log2 (n / 2)
65	
66	def build (pos : Array (Option Q)) : GapMax :=
67	  let n := pos.size
68	  let g : Array Q := (Array.range (n - 1)).map fun k =>
69	    match pos[k]?, pos[k + 1]? with
70	    | some (some a), some (some b) => Q.sub b a
71	    | _, _ => Q.zero
72	  let levels := log2 (max 1 g.size) + 1
73	  let table := (List.range levels).foldl (fun (acc : Array (Array Q)) k =>
74	    if k == 0 then #[g]
75	    else

97	    the window (an observation precedes it, or the oldest is exactly `d` behind), and whether the
98	    observations inside are at most `d/2` apart. -/

116	    let v := if (pos[i]?).getD none |>.isNone then i else acc[i + 1]!

126	  -- observedBefore[j]: some position at an index < j is observed
127	  let observedBefore : Array Bool := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Bool) j =>
128	    acc.push (acc[j]! || (pos[j]!).isSome)) #[false]

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Time
  Metric windows without a frame rate.

  Every observation carries a timestamp; a body also carries the path length it has travelled.
  A window is measured in one of the two: a duration of time, or a length of path travelled.
  Semantics are defined on the OBSERVED instants only; the one interpolation-free precondition is
  adequacy: a window of length d over a span is adequate when consecutive observations in the
  span are at most d/2 apart. An inadequate span yields `unknown`
  with the reason `samplingGap`, never a verdict invented between frames.

  Windows are computed for every instant of a trace at once: positions are monotone, so the
  window boundary moves one way and a two-pointer sweep with a range-maximum table over the gaps
  gives every window in O(n log n).

  There is no `next`, no rate and no frame count anywhere in the library.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Foundations.Units

namespace TrafficSpec

/-- Milliseconds, monotone within a trace. -/
abbrev Timestamp := Int

/-- Which quantity a window is measured in. -/
inductive Measure
  | time | path
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited

/-- A window: a non-negative length in seconds (time) or metres (path). -/
structure Duration where
  measure : Measure
  length : Q
  deriving Repr

namespace Duration
def time (q : Q) : Duration := ⟨.time, q⟩
def path (q : Q) : Duration := ⟨.path, q⟩
end Duration

namespace Time

def ofTimestamp (t : Timestamp) : Q := Units.milliseconds t

/-- Consecutive gaps of a sorted list of positions (time or path). -/
def gaps : List Q → List Q
  | a :: b :: rest => Q.sub b a :: gaps (b :: rest)
  | _ => []

/-- Every consecutive gap in the span is at most `d / 2`. Vacuously true on one observation. -/
def adequate (d : Q) (span : List Q) : Bool :=
  (gaps span).all (fun g => Q.le g (Q.half d))

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Range maximum over the gaps between consecutive observed positions (sparse table).
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- `gapMax.query lo hi` is the largest gap `pos[k] - pos[k-1]` for `lo < k ≤ hi`, given that
    every position in `[lo, hi]` is observed. -/
structure GapMax where
  table : Array (Array Q)      -- table[k][j] = max of gaps[j .. j + 2^k)
  gapsArr : Array Q            -- gapsArr[k] = pos[k+1] - pos[k], or zero where a side is missing

namespace GapMax
def log2 (n : Nat) : Nat := if n ≤ 1 then 0 else 1 + log2 (n / 2)

def build (pos : Array (Option Q)) : GapMax :=
  let n := pos.size
  let g : Array Q := (Array.range (n - 1)).map fun k =>
    match pos[k]?, pos[k + 1]? with
    | some (some a), some (some b) => Q.sub b a
    | _, _ => Q.zero
  let levels := log2 (max 1 g.size) + 1
  let table := (List.range levels).foldl (fun (acc : Array (Array Q)) k =>
    if k == 0 then #[g]
    else
      let prev := acc[k - 1]!
      let half := 2 ^ (k - 1)
      let row := (Array.range (prev.size)).map fun j =>
        if j + half < prev.size then Q.max prev[j]! prev[j + half]! else prev[j]!
      acc.push row) #[]
  ⟨table, g⟩

/-- Largest gap among the observations `lo, …, hi` (`lo < hi`); zero for a single observation. -/
def query (m : GapMax) (lo hi : Nat) : Q :=
  if hi ≤ lo then Q.zero
  else
    let len := hi - lo                  -- gaps indices lo … hi-1
    let k := log2 len
    let row := m.table[k]!
    Q.max row[lo]! row[hi - 2 ^ k]!
end GapMax

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Windows for every instant
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The window behind an instant: the oldest in-window index, whether the trace reaches back past
    the window (an observation precedes it, or the oldest is exactly `d` behind), and whether the
    observations inside are at most `d/2` apart. -/
structure Back where
  j0 : Nat
  covered : Bool
  adequate : Bool
  deriving Repr

/-- The window ahead of an instant, symmetrically. -/
structure Fwd where
  jl : Nat
  covered : Bool
  adequate : Bool
  deriving Repr

/-- Index of the earliest missing position at or after `i`, per instant (size n+1; `n` when none). -/
private def nextMissing (pos : Array (Option Q)) : Array Nat :=
  let n := pos.size
  (List.range n).reverse.foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
    let v := if (pos[i]?).getD none |>.isNone then i else acc[i + 1]!
    acc.set! i v) (Array.replicate (n + 1) n)

/-- Every back window of length `d`. `none` where the instant's own position or a position inside
    its window is missing (a gap the adequacy test could not see). Covered means an observed
    position precedes the window, or its oldest observation is exactly `d` behind. -/
def backWindows (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) : Array (Option Back) :=
  let n := pos.size
  let gm := GapMax.build pos
  let nm := nextMissing pos
  -- observedBefore[j]: some position at an index < j is observed
  let observedBefore : Array Bool := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Bool) j =>
    acc.push (acc[j]! || (pos[j]!).isSome)) #[false]
  let step (st : Nat × Array (Option Back)) (i : Nat) : Nat × Array (Option Back) :=
    let (j0, out) := st
    match pos[i]! with
    | none => (j0, out.push none)
    | some pi =>
      -- advance the oldest index while its position is observed and more than d behind
      let rec adv (j : Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Nat :=
        match fuel with
        | 0 => j
        | fuel + 1 =>
          if j ≥ i then j
          else match pos[j]! with
            | some pj => if Q.gt (Q.sub pi pj) d then adv (j + 1) fuel else j
            | none => adv (j + 1) fuel
      let j0' := adv j0 (i + 1 - j0)
      -- a missing position between j0' and i makes the window unknown
      if nm[j0']! ≤ i then (j0', out.push none)
      else
        let p0 := (pos[j0']!).getD pi
        let covered := observedBefore[j0']! || Q.ge (Q.sub pi p0) d
        let adequate := Q.le (gm.query j0' i) (Q.half d)
        (j0', out.push (some ⟨j0', covered, adequate⟩))
  ((List.range n).foldl step (0, Array.mkEmpty n)).2

/-- Every forward window of length `d`, by the same sweep run backwards. -/
def forwardWindows (pos : Array (Option Q)) (d : Q) : Array (Option Fwd) :=
  let n := pos.size
  let gm := GapMax.build pos
  -- observedFrom[j]: some position at an index ≥ j is observed (size n+1; false at n)
  let observedFrom : Array Bool := (List.range n).reverse.foldl (fun (acc : Array Bool) j =>
    acc.set! j (acc[j + 1]! || (pos[j]!).isSome)) (Array.replicate (n + 1) false)
  -- index of the latest missing position at or before i (n when none), per instant
  let lastMissing : Array Nat := (List.range n).foldl (fun (acc : Array Nat) i =>
    let v := if (pos[i]!).isNone then i else (if i = 0 then n else acc[i - 1]!)
    acc.push v) (Array.mkEmpty n)
  let step (st : Nat × List (Option Fwd)) (i : Nat) : Nat × List (Option Fwd) :=
    let (jl, out) := st
    match pos[i]! with
    | none => (jl, none :: out)
    | some pi =>
      let rec adv (j : Nat) (fuel : Nat) : Nat :=
        match fuel with
        | 0 => j
        | fuel + 1 =>
          if j ≤ i then j
          else match pos[j]! with
            | some pj => if Q.gt (Q.sub pj pi) d then adv (j - 1) fuel else j
            | none => adv (j - 1) fuel
      let jl' := adv jl (jl + 1 - i)
      let lm := lastMissing[jl']!
      if lm ≠ n && lm ≥ i then (jl', none :: out)
      else
        let pl := (pos[jl']!).getD pi
        let covered := observedFrom[jl' + 1]! || Q.ge (Q.sub pl pi) d
        let adequate := Q.le (gm.query i jl') (Q.half d)
        (jl', (some ⟨jl', covered, adequate⟩) :: out)
  (((List.range n).reverse).foldl step (n - 1, [])).2.toArray

end Time
end TrafficSpec

8	  the per-grounding timeline of verdicts.

10	  A track is a source's identity, not an object's. When a tracker breaks and the adapter claims a
11	  continuation (`Scene.links`, old ↦ new), the trace is rewritten once to canonical identities
12	  when the break is shorter than the manifest's re-identification gap; the instants inside the gap

14	  instant outside any gap leaves the rule not engaged there: the other party has left the scene.

17	  grounding evaluates the rule once over the whole trace, and formulas that depend on a subset of

22	import TrafficSpec.Core.Language.RuleEval

25	namespace TrafficSpec
26	namespace Grounding
27	open Semantics
28	
29	/-- An assignment of canonical tracks to binder names, and of regions to the variables a
30	    concept's instance takes as region formals (a rule's groundings bind none). -/
31	structure Grounding where
32	  assign : List (String × TrackId)
33	  regions : List (String × RegionId) := []
34	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
35	
36	def Grounding.render (g : Grounding) : String :=
37	  String.intercalate "," (g.assign.map fun (n, t) => s!"{n}={t}")
38	def Grounding.binding (g : Grounding) : Binding :=
39	  ⟨g.assign.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Val.track t)) ++ g.regions.map fun (n, r) => (n, Val.region r)⟩
40	
41	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
42	-- Identity: canonical tracks through accepted links, applied to the trace once
43	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
44	/-- The scene with every track id replaced by its canonical identity. -/
45	def canonicalScene (cm : List (TrackId × TrackId)) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
46	  let c := canon cm
47	  { s with
48	    subject := s.subject.map c
49	    users := s.users.map fun u => { u with track := c u.track }
50	    occupancyObserved := s.occupancyObserved.map c
51	    occupies := s.occupies.map fun (t, r) => (c t, r)
52	    relations := s.relations.map fun m => { m with a := c m.a, b := c m.b }
53	    intents := s.intents.map fun d => { d with vehicle := c d.vehicle } }
54	
55	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
56	-- Setup: the canonical, indexed trace and the rule set
57	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
58	structure Setup where
59	  rules : List Rule
60	  d : Primitives.Ctx
61	  gap : Q
62	  cm : List (TrackId × TrackId) := []
63	
64	def Setup.mk' (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Setup :=
65	  let arr := τ.toArray
66	  let cm := canonMap arr gap
67	  { rules := rules, d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' (τ.map (canonicalScene cm)) ρ, gap := gap, cm := cm }
68	
69	/-- The setup of a trace every evaluation reaches: built only when `Admission.defects` finds no
70	    defect in the trace as written, else the defects. -/
71	def Setup.admit (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Except (List String) Setup :=
72	  match Admission.defects τ gap with
73	  | [] => .ok (Setup.mk' rules τ ρ gap)
74	  | ds => .error ds

76	def Setup.n (S : Setup) : Nat := S.d.n
77	def Setup.scenes (S : Setup) : Array Scene := S.d.scenes
78	def Setup.ctx (S : Setup) (β : Binding) : SemCtx := Rule.context S.rules S.d β
79	def Setup.tracks (S : Setup) : List TrackId := (S.scenes.toList.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
80	/-- First and last instant at which a canonical identity is present. -/
81	def Setup.span (S : Setup) (t : TrackId) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
82	  match firstSeen S.scenes t, lastSeen S.scenes t with
83	  | some a, some b => some (a, b)
84	  | _, _ => none

87	-- Enumeration
88	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
89	/-- Tracks that satisfy a binder's class at some instant (evaluated once per track). -/
90	def candidates (S : Setup) (b : Binder) : List TrackId :=
91	  S.tracks.filter fun t =>
92	    (Rule.evalRuleFormula (S.ctx ⟨[(b.name, .track t)]⟩) b.cls).any fun r => r.v == .t

95	  match S.span a, S.span b with
96	  | some (a0, a1), some (b0, b1) => a0 ≤ b1 && b0 ≤ a1
97	  | _, _ => false

100	    Each binder's candidates are computed once. -/
101	def groundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List Grounding :=
102	  let cands := r.binders.map fun b => (b.name, candidates S b)
103	  let rec go (bs : List (String × List TrackId)) (used : List TrackId) : List (List (String × TrackId)) :=
104	    match bs with
105	    | [] => [[]]
106	    | (name, cs) :: rest =>
107	      cs.filter (fun c => !used.contains c && used.all (spansOverlap S c)) |>.flatMap fun c =>
108	        (go rest (c :: used)).map fun tail => (name, c) :: tail
109	  (go cands []).map fun a => { assign := a }
110	
111	/-- Predicted grounding count without enumerating: the product of candidate counts (an upper
112	    bound when candidates overlap). -/
113	def predictedGroundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Nat :=
114	  r.binders.foldl (fun acc b => acc * (candidates S b).length) 1

120	    engaged at some instant with every party present, and whether every party was present at
121	    some instant at all. -/
122	structure Timeline where
123	  verdicts : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
124	  live : Bool
125	  present : Bool
126	  deriving Repr

128	/-- Evaluate a rule for a grounding once. A binder absent inside its identity's span is an
129	    identity gap (unknown); absent outside it, the rule is not engaged. -/
130	def evaluate (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Timeline :=
131	  let c := S.ctx g.binding
132	  let engaged := r.engagedAll c
133	  let obl := Rule.evalRuleFormula c r.obligation
134	  let spans := g.assign.map fun (_, t) => (t, S.span t)
135	  let rows := (Array.range S.n).map fun i =>
136	    let s := S.scenes[i]!
137	    let missing := spans.filter fun (t, _) => !s.tracks.contains t
138	    let v : Verdict :=
139	      if missing.isEmpty then verdictAt engaged[i]! obl[i]!
140	      else
141	        let inGap := missing.filter fun (_, sp) => match sp with
142	          | some (a, b) => a < i && i < b
143	          | none => false
144	        if inGap.isEmpty then .notApplicable
145	        else .unknown (inGap.map fun (t, _) => .identityGap t)
146	    (s.t, v, missing.isEmpty && engaged[i]!.v == .t, missing.isEmpty)
147	  ⟨rows.map fun (t, v, _, _) => (t, v), rows.any fun (_, _, l, _) => l, rows.any fun (_, _, _, p) => p⟩

150

153	  ((timeline S r g)[i]?).map (·.2) |>.getD (.unknown [.outOfRange])
154	
155	/-- The episode verdict: a violation anywhere is a violation; else any unknown is unknown (with
156	    every reason); else engaged anywhere is compliant; else not applicable. -/
157	def episode (tl : List Verdict) : Verdict :=
158	  if tl.any (· == .violated) then .violated
159	  else
160	    let unknowns := tl.flatMap Verdict.reasons
161	    if tl.any (fun v => match v with | .unknown _ => true | _ => false) then .unknown unknowns.eraseDups
162	    else if tl.any (· == .compliant) then .compliant
163	    else .notApplicable
164	
165	/-- Every grounding evaluated once: its episode verdict and timeline. -/
166	def check (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List (Grounding × Timeline × Verdict) :=
167	  (groundings S r).map fun g =>
168	    let tl := evaluate S r g
169	    (g, tl, episode (tl.verdicts.toList.map (·.2)))
170	
171	/-- Engaged (applicability true) at some instant for some grounding: the rule says something on
172	    this trace. -/
173	def live (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Bool := (check S r).any fun (_, tl, _) => tl.live
174	
175	end Grounding
176	end TrafficSpec

def Grounding.render (g : Grounding) : String :=
  String.intercalate "," (g.assign.map fun (n, t) => s!"{n}={t}")
def Grounding.binding (g : Grounding) : Binding :=
  ⟨g.assign.map (fun (n, t) => (n, Val.track t)) ++ g.regions.map fun (n, r) => (n, Val.region r)⟩

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Identity: canonical tracks through accepted links, applied to the trace once
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- The scene with every track id replaced by its canonical identity. -/
def canonicalScene (cm : List (TrackId × TrackId)) (s : Scene) : Scene :=
  let c := canon cm
  { s with
    subject := s.subject.map c
    users := s.users.map fun u => { u with track := c u.track }
    occupancyObserved := s.occupancyObserved.map c
    occupies := s.occupies.map fun (t, r) => (c t, r)
    relations := s.relations.map fun m => { m with a := c m.a, b := c m.b }
    intents := s.intents.map fun d => { d with vehicle := c d.vehicle } }

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Setup: the canonical, indexed trace and the rule set
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
structure Setup where
  rules : List Rule
  d : Primitives.Ctx
  gap : Q
  cm : List (TrackId × TrackId) := []

def Setup.mk' (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Setup :=
  let arr := τ.toArray
  let cm := canonMap arr gap
  { rules := rules, d := Primitives.Ctx.mk' (τ.map (canonicalScene cm)) ρ, gap := gap, cm := cm }

/-- The setup of a trace every evaluation reaches: built only when `Admission.defects` finds no
    defect in the trace as written, else the defects. -/
def Setup.admit (rules : List Rule) (τ : Trace) (ρ : Reading) (gap : Q) : Except (List String) Setup :=
  match Admission.defects τ gap with
  | [] => .ok (Setup.mk' rules τ ρ gap)
  | ds => .error ds

def Setup.n (S : Setup) : Nat := S.d.n
def Setup.scenes (S : Setup) : Array Scene := S.d.scenes
def Setup.ctx (S : Setup) (β : Binding) : SemCtx := Rule.context S.rules S.d β
def Setup.tracks (S : Setup) : List TrackId := (S.scenes.toList.flatMap (·.tracks)).eraseDups
/-- First and last instant at which a canonical identity is present. -/
def Setup.span (S : Setup) (t : TrackId) : Option (Nat × Nat) :=
  match firstSeen S.scenes t, lastSeen S.scenes t with
  | some a, some b => some (a, b)
  | _, _ => none

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Enumeration
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- Tracks that satisfy a binder's class at some instant (evaluated once per track). -/
def candidates (S : Setup) (b : Binder) : List TrackId :=
  S.tracks.filter fun t =>
    (Rule.evalRuleFormula (S.ctx ⟨[(b.name, .track t)]⟩) b.cls).any fun r => r.v == .t

def spansOverlap (S : Setup) (a b : TrackId) : Bool :=
  match S.span a, S.span b with
  | some (a0, a1), some (b0, b1) => a0 ≤ b1 && b0 ≤ a1
  | _, _ => false

/-- All assignments of distinct, pairwise co-present candidates to the binders, subject first.
    Each binder's candidates are computed once. -/
def groundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List Grounding :=
  let cands := r.binders.map fun b => (b.name, candidates S b)
  let rec go (bs : List (String × List TrackId)) (used : List TrackId) : List (List (String × TrackId)) :=
    match bs with
    | [] => [[]]
    | (name, cs) :: rest =>
      cs.filter (fun c => !used.contains c && used.all (spansOverlap S c)) |>.flatMap fun c =>
        (go rest (c :: used)).map fun tail => (name, c) :: tail
  (go cands []).map fun a => { assign := a }

/-- Predicted grounding count without enumerating: the product of candidate counts (an upper
    bound when candidates overlap). -/
def predictedGroundings (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Nat :=
  r.binders.foldl (fun acc b => acc * (candidates S b).length) 1

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Timelines
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
/-- One evaluation of a rule for a grounding: the verdict per instant, whether the rule was
    engaged at some instant with every party present, and whether every party was present at
    some instant at all. -/
structure Timeline where
  verdicts : Array (Timestamp × Verdict)
  live : Bool
  present : Bool
  deriving Repr

/-- Evaluate a rule for a grounding once. A binder absent inside its identity's span is an
    identity gap (unknown); absent outside it, the rule is not engaged. -/
def evaluate (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Timeline :=
  let c := S.ctx g.binding
  let engaged := r.engagedAll c
  let obl := Rule.evalRuleFormula c r.obligation
  let spans := g.assign.map fun (_, t) => (t, S.span t)
  let rows := (Array.range S.n).map fun i =>
    let s := S.scenes[i]!
    let missing := spans.filter fun (t, _) => !s.tracks.contains t
    let v : Verdict :=
      if missing.isEmpty then verdictAt engaged[i]! obl[i]!
      else
        let inGap := missing.filter fun (_, sp) => match sp with
          | some (a, b) => a < i && i < b
          | none => false
        if inGap.isEmpty then .notApplicable
        else .unknown (inGap.map fun (t, _) => .identityGap t)
    (s.t, v, missing.isEmpty && engaged[i]!.v == .t, missing.isEmpty)
  ⟨rows.map fun (t, v, _, _) => (t, v), rows.any fun (_, _, l, _) => l, rows.any fun (_, _, _, p) => p⟩

def timeline (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) : Array (Timestamp × Verdict) := (evaluate S r g).verdicts

/-- The verdict of a grounding at one instant. -/
def verdictAt (S : Setup) (r : Rule) (g : Grounding) (i : Nat) : Verdict :=
  ((timeline S r g)[i]?).map (·.2) |>.getD (.unknown [.outOfRange])

/-- The episode verdict: a violation anywhere is a violation; else any unknown is unknown (with
    every reason); else engaged anywhere is compliant; else not applicable. -/
def episode (tl : List Verdict) : Verdict :=
  if tl.any (· == .violated) then .violated
  else
    let unknowns := tl.flatMap Verdict.reasons
    if tl.any (fun v => match v with | .unknown _ => true | _ => false) then .unknown unknowns.eraseDups
    else if tl.any (· == .compliant) then .compliant
    else .notApplicable

/-- Every grounding evaluated once: its episode verdict and timeline. -/
def check (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : List (Grounding × Timeline × Verdict) :=
  (groundings S r).map fun g =>
    let tl := evaluate S r g
    (g, tl, episode (tl.verdicts.toList.map (·.2)))

/-- Engaged (applicability true) at some instant for some grounding: the rule says something on
    this trace. -/
def live (S : Setup) (r : Rule) : Bool := (check S r).any fun (_, tl, _) => tl.live

end Grounding
end TrafficSpec

/-
  TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Admission
  What a trace must satisfy, as written, before any rule is evaluated on it: the declared facts
  (assumptions and intentions) name what their scene holds, each once, by well-formed ids; no
  structure is labelled with an abstract kind or lists one among the kinds its source cannot tell
  (an abstract kind is the union of the kinds refining it, read only by a formula); and the
  accepted re-identification links are one-to-one.

  The checks are exact and read no geometry, so a recorded trace, a JSON case and a Lean witness
  are held to them alike. `Grounding.Setup.admit` calls them; every evaluation builds its setup
  there.
-/
import TrafficSpec.Core.Runtime.Identity
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Assumptions
import TrafficSpec.Core.Vocab.Intentions

namespace TrafficSpec
namespace Admission

private def duplicates {α : Type} [BEq α] (xs : List α) : List α :=
  (xs.filter fun x => xs.count x > 1).eraseDups

/-- The defects of one scene's declared facts. -/
def sceneDefects (s : Scene) : List String :=
  let at_ := s!"scene t={s.t}"
  (s.intents.flatMap fun d =>
    let who := s!"{at_}: intent record ({d.vehicle}, {d.target})"
    (if s.tracks.contains d.vehicle then [] else [s!"{who}: vehicle {d.vehicle} is not a road user of the scene"]) ++
    (if (s.structure? d.target).isSome then [] else [s!"{who}: target {d.target} is not a structure of the scene"]) ++
    ((duplicates (d.values.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` listed more than once") ++
    ((d.values.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!IntId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{who}: `{id}` is not a well-formed intention id")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.intents.map fun d => (d.vehicle, d.target))).map fun (v, r) => s!"{at_}: more than one intent record for ({v}, {r})") ++
  (s.structures.flatMap fun st =>
    (if st.kind.isAbstract then [s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} is labelled `{st.kind}`, an abstract kind; label it with a kind that refines `{st.kind}`"] else []) ++
    ((st.unobservedKinds.filter (·.isAbstract)).eraseDups.map fun k =>
      s!"{at_}: structure {st.id} lists `{k}` among unobserved_kinds, an abstract kind; list the kinds refining it that the source cannot tell")) ++
  ((duplicates (s.assumptions.map (·.1))).map fun id => s!"{at_}: assumption `{id}` listed more than once") ++
  ((s.assumptions.map (·.1)).eraseDups.filter (!AsmId.wellFormed ·) |>.map fun id => s!"{at_}: `{id}` is not a well-formed assumption id")

/-- Accepted links that give a track two successors or two predecessors. -/
def linkDefects (τ : Array Scene) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  let links := Grounding.acceptedLinks τ gap
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.1))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} is continued by more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.1 == t)}") ++
  ((duplicates (links.map (·.2))).map fun t =>
    s!"track {t} continues more than one accepted link: {links.filter (·.2 == t)}")

/-- Every defect of the trace as written; empty for a trace every evaluation may read. -/
def defects (τ : Trace) (gap : Q) : List String :=
  τ.flatMap sceneDefects ++ linkDefects τ.toArray gap

end Admission
end TrafficSpec
